On-screen prompt / action: Possible collapse detected or reported. ALERT nearby crew and open the emergency check-in: 'Possible collapse. Are you okay? Please respond.' Do not let an unanswered app prompt delay hands-on response.
Engineer / clinical note: Detection limp duration: NOT YET AGREED with Jion. Simulated event only; no camera-only diagnosis.

On-screen prompt / action: Does the crewmember respond to voice or gentle touch?
Engineer / clinical note: Protect rescuer and patient from drifting or collision.

On-screen prompt / action: Is there chest pain, breathing difficulty, fainting, severe injury, or marked confusion after the event?
Engineer / clinical note: Even if responsive, suspected fall may need medical review.

On-screen prompt / action: Is the unresponsive crewmember breathing normally? (Gasping is NOT normal breathing.)
Engineer / clinical note: Rapid breathing assessment; activate crew medical emergency response.

On-screen prompt / action: UNRESPONSIVE BUT BREATHING: secure the person in a safe position appropriate to the habitat; monitor breathing continuously and request immediate crew medical intervention. Do not give food, drink or medication by mouth.
Engineer / clinical note: Airway positioning is per crew medical training and mission protocol.

On-screen prompt / action: For a trained medical responder only: is a definite pulse found within 10 seconds?
Engineer / clinical note: If unsure/no definite pulse: choose NO. A PPG pulse-loss signal alone is not cardiac-arrest diagnosis.

On-screen prompt / action: PULSE PRESENT, NOT BREATHING NORMALLY: initiate crew medical respiratory-arrest protocol and trained rescue ventilation, reassessing pulse and breathing per medical guidance. Escalate to flight surgeon immediately.
Engineer / clinical note: Crew medical training governs ventilation and airway equipment.

On-screen prompt / action: NO DEFINITE PULSE AND NOT BREATHING NORMALLY: start CPR immediately, call for AED and crew medical kit. Adult BLS target: 100–120 compressions/min, 5–6 cm depth on firm surface, full recoil; trained rescuers use ventilation per BLS. Do NOT delay CPR waiting for ground contact.
Engineer / clinical note: In microgravity, trained rescuers may use Evetts–Russomano initially and transition to approved medical restraint system; actual procedure requires mission training.

On-screen prompt / action: Apply the available AED/defibrillator according to device instructions and the approved crew medical procedure. Minimize pauses in CPR and follow device prompts; ensure patient/rescuer anchoring in microgravity.
Engineer / clinical note: Do not invent device settings or medication doses.

On-screen prompt / action: Has the crewmember clearly regained responsiveness and normal breathing?
Engineer / clinical note: No automatic confirmation from sensor alone.

On-screen prompt / action: Severe symptoms or injury after a collapse: activate crew medical response now; if chest pain, enter chest-pain protocol CP00. Keep patient secured and continue assessment.
Urgency: Flight surgeon now + crew medical response
Engineer / clinical note: Route CP00 only after urgent stabilization.

On-screen prompt / action: Responsive after suspected collapse without reported red flags: crew medical officer assesses possible fall/syncope and sensor false-positive. Do not automatically authorize an EVA or high-risk task.
Ongoing emergency care: keep patient under direct crew observation, maintain appropriate support and monitoring, document event and consult flight surgeon now when communication permits.
Urgency: Flight surgeon now + ongoing onboard care
Engineer / clinical note: Never rely on an Earth round-trip before immediate treatment.

On-screen prompt / action: Continue resuscitation according to trained crew medical responders and AED prompts until approved stopping criteria are met or reassessment directs otherwise; rotate rescuers if possible.
Engineer / clinical note: This loop is a demo workflow, not an autonomous clinical stop rule.
